authority: Owner decision 2026-09-23. These are governed release-policy assertions, not a rigid code freeze: each carries an explicit reclassification trigger so a future legitimate feature is possible through a deliberate policy/version change rather than accidental drift.

maintainer_intent.note: The 0.9.x core release is free/open source. Possible future monetization is not part of this release's operating behaviour and must not be inferred by consumers of this manifest.

invariants.statement: PX must not contact a PX-operated remote endpoint from core code.
invariants.evidence_surface: static host scan + live network trace
invariants.reclassification_trigger: introducing a PX-operated production endpoint requires a privacy/data-flow/compliance reclassification recorded in the applicability matrix before release

invariants.statement: Production PX and the extension must not emit remote telemetry.
invariants.evidence_surface: telemetry emitter scan; VS Code telemetry API usage
invariants.reclassification_trigger: introducing any production telemetry emitter requires a privacy/telemetry reclassification, an updated TELEMETRY.md, a telemetry manifest, and VS Code isTelemetryEnabled gating
invariants.clarification: Local operational logs, traces, certification evidence, and diagnostics that remain on the user's machine are NOT remote telemetry.

invariants.statement: PX must not download model weights without explicit user approval.
invariants.evidence_surface: download-call scan against the external-runtime policy
permitted_behaviours: explain where and how to obtain them
perform an explicitly approval-gated download step that first records model identity, source, license, revision, expected size, expected hash, destination and usage restrictions
invariants.reclassification_trigger: adding an automatic download path requires the approval gate above plus a model-license manifest entry

invariants.statement: No credential literal may ship in authored source.
invariants.evidence_surface: credential-shape scan (length + entropy + PEM + provider prefixes)
invariants.reclassification_trigger: none - this invariant is not relaxable; a real credential in the tree is a defect

invariants.statement: Shipped source must contain no developer/user-specific absolute path or personal identifier.
invariants.reclassification_trigger: none - portability is required for any installation on another machine
invariants.contact_allowlist_reason: The project's own published security contact must appear in SECURITY.md and the security/compliance documents that tell a reporter where to send a vulnerability. This is the project's own contact address, not a third party's personal identifier.

invariants.statement: Local failure must never silently grant permission to use a remote provider.
invariants.evidence_surface: routing/fallback policy and provider gateway admission
invariants.verification: runtime routing tests + provider adapter registry admission
invariants.reclassification_trigger: none - silent fallback to a remote provider is prohibited; explicit policy is required

invariants.statement: An external provider may be used only when the user has explicitly configured and authorized it.
invariants.reclassification_trigger: none - unconfigured providers remain denied by contract

invariants.statement: Introducing a PX-operated hosted service requires a compliance reclassification before it may become part of a release.
invariants.reclassification_trigger: this invariant IS the trigger; it fires on hosted-service introduction

invariants.statement: Introducing production telemetry requires a privacy/telemetry reclassification before it may become part of a release.
invariants.evidence_surface: applicability matrix entry + updated TELEMETRY.md + telemetry manifest

invariants.statement: Introducing a commercial or hosted feature requires a CRA/GDPR/state-law applicability review before it may become part of a release.

owner_decisions.decision: One-time explicit migration of a workspace / .vscode key-like value into VS Code SecretStorage; runtime access is exclusively through SecretStorage.
rules: treat the workspace value as a migration source only, never an operational credential source
do not silently consume a discovered credential during normal runtime
offer a bounded, user-initiated 'credential detected -> import?' action
verify retrieval from SecretStorage after storing
advise removal of the plaintext value; offer to scrub only if PX has authority over that exact config
never write the secret into logs, evidence, diagnostics, telemetry, exception text, state snapshots, or generated artifacts
store only non-secret status (configured=true, provider name, last validation timestamp)
if both SecretStorage and plaintext exist, SecretStorage wins and the plaintext copy raises a warning rather than acting as a fallback
owner_decisions.rejected_alternative: automatic migration without user interaction - that would mean PX reads and persists a credential based merely on discovery

owner_decisions.decision: PX exposes its own model/chat capability through the host-native LanguageModelChatProvider; PX retains routing authority, provider policy, task envelopes, budgets, retries/fallbacks, context construction, memory, evidence, approvals, orchestration, and result verification.
rules: consumers reach PX through the host provider interface
PX routes onward to local model / configured API model / explicit external adapters
external vendor agents only through explicit governed adapters, never arbitrary CLI worker assimilation
owner_decisions.rejected_alternative: commandeering vendor CLIs (Codex/Claude/Copilot) as obedient subprocess workers, which would import their authority and terms into PX

permitted_positioning: PX includes controls designed to support governed, auditable operation. Applicability and compliance depend on deployment context, enabled providers, data flows, and intended use.
